answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the volume it moves, like a pearl forming layer by layer around a grain of sand. Newcomers start with tiny limits, and their allowed flow widens only as they accumulate verified, costly history — a river that deepens slowly instead of flooding the meadow all at once. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand separate stakes, while honest agents earn their limits back through steady work.
